name: Copper John
imitates: A heavy, flashy generic mayfly and stonefly nymph; the go-to weighted point fly that gets a rig down fast.
recipe: White 14/0, colored black at the head
Flash and scud back material, UV resin

steps.text: Slide a countersunk bead on the hook, small hole first, and leave it at the eye.
With the hook locked in the vise, wrap 10-12 turns of lead wire behind the bead and push the coil snug against it.
Lock the thread on, then wrap back to the start of the bend, level with the barb.
Tie in a pair of goose biots as a forked tail, flared apart and about half the body length.
Tie in copper wire at the front of the abdomen, bring the thread to the tail, then wrap the wire forward in touching turns and tie it off.
Just behind the bead, tie in a strip of flash and a strip of scud back on top of the shank, running back over the abdomen.
Tie in two peacock herls with their tips trimmed even, just behind the bead.
Wrap the herl forward in tight turns with no gaps to form the thorax and tie it off at the bead.
Cut a V-notch in the tip of a hen feather and tie it in on top of the shank with the notch facing back for the legs, using loose wraps.
Pull the scud back forward over the thorax and secure it with loose wraps, then tug the feather base to shorten the legs to the right length.
Pull the flash over the wing case, secure it, and trim the flash, scud back and feather close to the bead.
Color the thread black with a marker, tidy the head with a few wraps, and whip finish twice.
Spread a couple of drops of UV resin over the wing case and the back of the bead and cure it with a UV torch.
